scope: P1 native Matrix gateway credential storage and recovery; no public gateway or admission wiring
behaviors: One retained company/account/native-parent/device head; hashes only, one AES-GCM response cache; public token values redact diagnostics.
Two concurrent refresh transactions produce one compare-and-set winner; lost-response replay returns that pair; a subsequent rotation rejects the older hash without revoking its device.
A new bootstrap updates the client build without replacing the device and invalidates earlier credentials and bootstrap replay.
Transaction-local lookup resolves only one opaque-token head and is absent on a reused connection after transaction completion; it does not itself grant HRIS admission.
Deadline tampering fails AEAD; a failed business Result rolls back a credential rotation.
Maintenance is bounded to 100 expired caches, skips a locked head, cannot alter active credentials or clear ahead of database time, and finishes after lock release.
SQL denies foreign parent/platform, excessive lifetimes, malformed replay, deletion, unrevoked retirement and generation resurrection.
Actual pg_dump/pg_restore preserves old/current key envelopes; the independent Python/SQL recovery projection decrypts both and matches Kotlin AAD.
